title: The Dark Panel
setting: A lighthouse on a rock, one night before the inspection is signed

victim.name: Hollis Brandt
victim.summary: Head keeper of Gannet Rock, found dead on the lamp-room floor.

brief: Hollis Brandt kept the Gannet Rock light for twenty-two years. At eleven that night the lamp went dark. The assistant keeper and the inspector climbed the tower and found him on the lamp-room floor. Four others had been on the rock that night.

suspects.name: Wren Doyle
suspects.relation: Worked beside Hollis for six years
suspects.alibi: Says she was in the kitchen all night with the inspector.
suspects.note: Tired, tied to the log book.

suspects.name: Iris Venn
suspects.relation: Came out two weeks ago to service the lens
suspects.alibi: Says she was in the workshop until the lamp went dark.

suspects.name: Callum Pryce
suspects.alibi: Says he was aboard his boat from nine.
suspects.note: Loud. Owes money in every port.

suspects.name: Marta Quill
suspects.relation: Here to sign off the yearly inspection
suspects.alibi: Says she played cards with Wren.

items.title: Who held the keys
items.body: Hollis, Wren and Iris each held a tower key. Callum and Marta held none. The tower door was found on the latch.

lines.a: In the kitchen with Marta, playing cards. We did not leave until the lamp went dark.
Steps came down the tower stairs not long after ten. Quick and light. Then the workshop door shut. I thought it was Hollis.
In the workshop from half past nine, cleaning prisms. I never left the ground floor.
At supper. He said he would check the lens at ten. Nothing more.

lines.q: When did you leave the rock?
lines.a: Nine. I crossed the causeway to my boat and stayed aboard.
He paid me last month. We were square.

lines.q: Who were you with at ten?
lines.a: Wren, at cards, in the kitchen. I wrote down the hands from habit.
He was short with everyone. He said the lens needed a hard look.
Someone came quick down the tower stairs, then the workshop door shut. Wren heard it too.

sections.heading: Cause
sections.body: One blow to the back of the head from a heavy narrow bar.

sections.heading: Time
sections.body: Between ten and eleven at night.

sections.heading: Stairs and gallery rail
sections.body: Both sound. No marks of a fall.

sections.heading: Lamp room
sections.body: The lens still turns. A damp rag lies by the door, with a grey paste that smells of spirit. The wick is burnt dry. No one trimmed it after ten.

sections.heading: Door
sections.body: Tower door on the latch. No force used.

items.caption: Hollis lay beside the lens. The middle panel of the lens is plain flat glass, with no prism cut.

items.title: Brass bar
items.body: A heavy brass bar was pushed behind the lamp-room oil drum and wiped. Its grip is wound with blue cloth tape, the same tape that hangs in the workshop.

items.title: Hollis's log page
items.body: Counted the lens again by glass. The middle panel rings dull. It is plain glass, not a prism. Someone has swapped it. I will ask the engineer in the lamp room at ten.

items.title: Dealer's letter
items.body: Dear Ms Venn: we accept the cut prisms at the price agreed. Lens grade, no chips. Payment on collection at Harbour Salvage.

rows.text: Supper in the kitchen. All five sit down. Hollis says he will check the lens at ten.
Callum crosses the causeway to his boat.
Hollis climbs the tower. Wren and Marta start cards in the kitchen.
Callum radios from his boat. Marta answers.
The lamp goes dark. Wren and Marta climb together and find Hollis.

items.caption: The tower stands between the kitchen and the workshop. The causeway runs from the workshop side to the jetty.

items.title: Tide table
items.body: The tide covers the causeway from ten at night until midnight. No one crosses in either direction.

motives.text: Hollis refused a place on the new lens contract.
The lens prisms were sold, and Hollis found out.
Hollis would not lend any more money.
Hollis meant to report someone to the board.

methods.text: Pushed him down the tower stairs.
One blow to the back of the head.
Cut the gallery rail so he fell.
